original_question: What is the correct analog of the asymptotic lower matching conjecture for infinite cubic connected graphs with no bridges? Equivalently, what lower-entropy statement should replace the bipartite ALMC in the bridgeless infinite 3-regular setting?
target_in_paper: Section 7, final unnumbered open problem: 'Second, what is the analog of the ALMC for infinite cubic connected graphs with no bridges?'
correct_elements: Your draft is already very close to the paper's actual target. It correctly identifies that the issue is an asymptotic lower matching question for infinite graphs, not a finite counting problem; it keeps the paper's key hypotheses 'infinite', 'cubic', 'connected', and 'no bridges'; and it correctly interprets the target as a lower-entropy replacement for the bipartite ALMC.
missing_details: The paper's standing graph convention is: undirected graphs with no loops, while multiple edges are allowed unless excluded; for the infinite setting, the graph has a countable vertex set.

The entropy object must be named explicitly: for a countable infinite graph G, the p-matching (monomer-dimer) entropy h_G(p) is defined via a sequence of finite graphs G_k converging to G and integers m_k with 2m_k/|V_k| -> p, by h_G(p)=limsup_{k->infinity} |V_k|^{-1} log phi(m_k,G_k), where phi(m_k,G_k) is the number of m_k-matchings.

The bipartite benchmark being replaced should be stated explicitly: ALMC says that for any r-regular bipartite infinite graph G, h_G(p) >= f(p,r) for all p in [0,1], where f(p,r)=1/2*(p log r - p log p - 2(1-p) log(1-p) + (r-p) log(1-p/r)).
The paper does not itself propose the non-bipartite cubic lower-bound function or a precise conjectural inequality; it leaves that as an open problem.

The final Section 7 question does not fix an exact p-range for the cubic bridgeless analogue; the introduction only says that a similar inequality for infinite non-bipartite r-regular graphs should exist at least in a certain range, so a stand-alone rewrite should not overstate a range the paper does not formally specify for this cubic bridgeless case.
The notion of convergence G_k -> G is not redefined in full in this paper; Section 1 refers the reader to [22] for the precise setup.

It helps to distinguish this from Conjecture 1.1: Conjecture 1.1 is the finite bridgeless-cubic perfect-matching growth problem, whereas your target is the infinite-graph entropy analogue posed later in Section 7.
refined_question: Let G be a countably infinite connected bridgeless 3-regular graph, under the paper's standing convention that graphs are undirected, loopless, and may have multiple edges. For p-monomer entropy defined by h_G(p)=limsup_{k->infinity} |V_k|^{-1} log phi(m_k,G_k) over finite graphs G_k converging to G with 2m_k/|V_k| -> p, the bipartite asymptotic lower matching conjecture asserts h_G(p) >= f(p,3), where f(p,3)=1/2*(p log 3 - p log p - 2(1-p) log(1-p) + (3-p) log(1-p/3)). What is the correct analogue of this lower-bound inequality for such non-bipartite bridgeless cubic graphs; equivalently, what explicit lower-entropy statement should replace the bipartite ALMC in the infinite connected bridgeless 3-regular setting?
justification: The draft is targeting the paper's last open problem in Section 7, not Conjecture 1.1 itself. Section 1 introduces the p-monomer entropy h_G(p), states the bipartite ALMC as the inequality h_G(p) >= f(p,r), and immediately notes that a similar inequality should exist for infinite non-bipartite r-regular graphs although the precise version is not known. Section 7 then specializes that missing analogue to the exact cubic bridgeless connected case by asking, verbatim, for the analog of ALMC there. So the sharpest paper-faithful rewrite is to ask for the explicit lower entropy inequality that should replace the bipartite bound h_G(p) >= f(p,3) for infinite connected bridgeless cubic graphs.
